load_bearing_primary.interpretation: A coverage budget is a question about how much of the ASK the model recognised. Charging the tokens of a stated path to it made the verdict depend on the length of the caller's file names rather than on the request. A capability whose own adapter names a module or program that is not there can only fail, so the dependency has to be declared before the refusal can be said early. But the RANKING is a fact about the model and not about the host: this sandbox has pypdf and the CI runner does not, so filtering the ranking by presence made a pinned route hold in one place and fail in the other. The host votes where the work happens -- in solve() -- and nowhere else.
load_bearing_primary.measured_effect: All ten measured sentences naming real absolute paths now route confidently; before, all ten were refused with GOAL_NOT_REPRESENTED_IN_MODEL__FAIL_CLOSED. Coverage on "count the functions defined in the python file <abs path> and write the report to <abs path>" went from 0.240 to 0.714 and is now identical to the same sentence with the paths deleted. Capabilities correctly reporting an unresolvable declared dependency went from 7 to 12 -- PIL x6, chromedriver, crosshair, pandoc, tesseract, pdftoppm, yq/yaml -- every one for a tool genuinely absent. The ranking is host-independent and pinned that way: with every declared dependency on the machine reported missing, 367 of 374 capabilities unrunnable, all four pinned known-goal routes are still confident and still land where the model says. solve() now names the missing dependency instead of spending the request and returning BOUND_PYPI_SOURCE_INCOMPLETE. 15 new tests, 12 of which fail on origin/main; the 3 that pass either way are the negative controls. Verifier 33/33, integrity guard 17/0, artifact byte-identical to a fresh recompile.

obs_blocker.delete_bypass_substitute_options: Letting the census answer and report pass=True was rejected: it reports a count of files for a request to create test files. Adding targets_path and generated_tests_root to the binder's phrasing tables was rejected: no sentence carries a manifest of which modules to cover, so the capability would stay unbindable for every phrasing an engineer writes. Requiring the caller to run the symbol index first and pass it as index_path was rejected: the adapter already builds that index internally when no cache is given, so it would be asking the caller to do work the callee does anyway. Installing pytest was rejected: it makes a bound capability depend on a third-party package to run a file the stdlib already owns, and the compiler must stay environment-independent. Emitting a pytest-style test file instead was rejected: the existing _render_module already emits unittest, which is the dependency-free form. Defaulting generated_tests_root to a directory inside source_root was rejected because the adapter's own PATH_OVERLAPS_SOURCE_ROOT law forbids it.
obs_blocker.intrinsic_or_path_specific: Path-specific to one adapter's argument handling and one registry template. Nothing new was invented: the index the adapter already builds supplies the targets, the adapter's own overlap law determines the default output location, unittest is already what _render_module emits, and #6272 established the convention that a template must not demand what the adapter defaults.

obs_capability.external_existing_routes_checked: No external source was needed.  sed's `r`, `find -name`, `find -type f` and `ls` on one level are ordinary POSIX behaviour and each was probed directly in this environment before a rule was written.

obs_goal.real_outcome: An append appends, a tree question walks the tree, a count is not answered with names, and the plainest form of each works.
obs_goal.surviving_necessity: The operation has to be the one the sentence stated, and a two-file promise has to be asked of both files afterwards.

obs_inherited_system.fresh_reuse_plan: Reuse sed's r command, the find rule's existing -name construction, `_post_sort`'s recompute-from-a-surviving-source model, and the count-versus-listing distinction entire; add one routing rule, widen and scope one entry condition, add one postcondition shape and one refusal.

obs_obs.search_stop_decision: Stop: the sixteen-row census is thirteen of sixteen with zero certified wrong answers and zero destructive rows, and every new postcondition is pinned able to fail.  Measured and deliberately left unserved: the first line of two files at once, a line count over two files, sorting two files together, the lines in both files, the lines in one that are not in the other, and whether one file is larger than another -- each needs a pipeline or an arithmetic comparison, and no single program here does either.

obs_solution.losing_routes_reason: Adding an append-mode writer to the registry loses because it adds a producer to trust where a command and a postcondition suffice.  Refusing the append loses because sed's `r` command performs it and the source survives to prove it.  Widening `find` on the word 'named' alone loses on measurement twice: it answered a deletion of a matched set, and a creation of a folder, with a listing.  Answering a count with `ls` loses because a list of names is not a number and was certified as one.
routes_ranked: sed's r command wins over an append-mode writer, because the source survives and the promise is recomputable
recomputing the promised tail from the source wins over trusting the run, for the reason _post_sort already established
widening the find entry condition wins over adding a second tree rule, because the rule already built -name correctly
scoping the widening away from mutation and creation verbs wins over keying on the word alone, measured both ways
refusing a count of a directory wins over answering it with ls, because a list of names is not a number
comparing the world afterwards wins over comparing the answer, because the defect was a file that no longer existed

obs_verification.synthetic_verification_necessity: Not synthetic: the census runs the real command in a parallel directory and compares BOTH its stdout and the resulting tree file by file, so a row that destroys a file cannot pass however plausible its answer looks -- which is exactly the defect that started this.  The append is asserted on the bytes the destination held as well as the bytes added, and the source is asserted unchanged, so a copy cannot pass as an append.  The postcondition is pinned able to fail from both sides, including a source outside the repository.  The two regressions the widening caused are pinned closed by a deletion that must stay refused with the file still there, and a creation that must still create.

route_frontier.negative_search_summary: Widening the make...upper window from 20 to 200 characters was rejected as the same rule with a bigger number: it would still be a distance, it would still be wrong for a long enough path, and it would widen every sentence the window was keeping out. Masking the operand is what the blank arm in the same block already does, so this reuses a mechanism rather than inventing one. Adding 'not' to `_NEGATED_LINE` itself was rejected: that pattern is scoped to contain/match/include and is used by the VALUE arms, so widening it would invert value questions nobody measured. Inverting on the bare word 'not' was rejected -- 'the lines that are not blank' and 'the lines that are not sorted' are different questions and only the first is about blankness, so the negation is anchored to blank|empty. Fixing all 13 window-shaped rules at once was rejected as unmeasured: only the one that produced a certified wrong answer was fixed, and the rest are recorded as an open item with their count rather than being changed on suspicion. All alternatives DISQUALIFIED on measured grounds.

BROAD_WEB_OR_COMMUNITY: https://api.github.com/search/repositories?q=postcondition%20verify%20effect%20not%20rerun -- a mutating command is verified by the state it left, never by running it twice; no standalone project owns the rule because it is a property of the check
CODE_OR_PACKAGE_REGISTRY: https://pypi.org/pypi/astunparse/json and the standard library's own compile() error handling -- both treat a parse failure as a property of one input rather than a fatal condition for the caller
